what_changed_today: PRICE RECLAIMED THE 50-DAY AND THE FIB BAND: close 7,489.72 (+~0.7% vs prior 7,437.63) is now above the 50-day (7,471.5), the 61.8% (7,467.43), 50% (7,478.60) and 38.2% (7,489.77) retracements, and is pressing the 23.6% fib at 7,503.60 — a fourth consecutive up-session and full recovery of the 7/29 breakdown.

VIX COLLAPSED TO 15.99 FROM 17.09, dropping below its 50-day MA (~17.5) to the bottom of the standard operating band — the most complacent reading of the arc and the opposite of a capitulation-spike re-entry signal.

MONTE CARLO REBALANCED TO NEAR-COIN-FLIP BUT STILL DOWN-FIRST: adjusted prob_up_first 43.92% vs 56.08% down-first (from 62.54% up-first prior), with median 3 days up / 2 days down as the targets have compressed to 7,525.94 upside and 7,478.60 downside — a seventh straight session failing all regime thresholds (65/70/75).
VALUATION TIGHTENED AGAIN: 10-year rose to 4.745% and ERP slipped to 0.32% (from 0.43%), keeping the market in the 0.0-0.5% valuation-ceiling band with the re-entry floor down at 7,225.93.

SHORT-TERM MOMENTUM CONFIRMED, PARTICIPATION DID NOT: 5-day MFI has surged to ~83 (above the 80 trim line) and daily RSI is back to ~52-62, while McClellan breadth (856.63, score 23) sits at its cycle-low reference and net new highs slid to 1.18 (score 30).
narrative_summary: SPX closed 7,489.72 after a fourth straight advance, reclaiming the 50-day and the entire 7,467-7,490 fib cluster and erasing the 7/29 breakdown — a genuine short-term structural improvement. But the recovery is arriving with the weakest internal confirmation of the arc: McClellan breadth is at its cycle-low reference, net new highs have fallen to 1.18, ERP has slipped to 0.32% at the valuation ceiling, and the 5-day MFI is already in the >80 trim zone. Monte Carlo has rebalanced to a near coin flip (43.9% up-first vs 56.1% down-first) against compressed targets and still fails the 70% Late Bull threshold for a seventh session. The regime stays Late Bull / Topping: reclaim the resistance band, sell strength into 7,504-7,526, and demand breadth confirmation before treating this as anything more than a rally into supply.
open_questions: Can price close above the 23.6% fib (7,503.60) and the 7,525.94 swing high on expanding breadth, or does the SMA/fib band cap the move and produce a lower high?
Will McClellan breadth (856.63, cycle-low reference) and net new highs (1.18) finally turn up to confirm four days of price gains, or does narrowing participation confirm the topping process?

Does the ERP slide to 0.32% on a 4.745% 10-year cap upside multiple expansion even if earnings hold?

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Price has reclaimed the 50-day and full fib band in four sessions; breadth is a lagging series that typically turns up after price confirms, and the McClellan index is basing near a level that has marked prior tradable lows.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: McClellan Volume Summation sits at 856.63 (score 23) at its cycle-low reference and net new 52-week highs have slid to 1.18 (score 30) even as price rallies four days into resistance — falling participation into a recovery near the highs is the textbook narrow-leadership topping warning.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down; falling sentiment/participation near new highs is a topping warning.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: The down-first skew is a mechanical artifact of target compression — the 50% fib downside target (7,478.60) sits only 11 points below spot while the swing high is 36 points above, so a 56/44 split is near-neutral rather than genuinely bearish.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Adjusted prob_up_first of 43.92% fails the 65%, 70% and 75% thresholds for a seventh straight session, median days are 2 down vs 3 up, and the conditional cascade shows a 98% chance of reaching 7,467 if 7,479 breaks — the edge is simply not there for deployment.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Never use the Monte Carlo output in isolation; if the adjusted probability does not meet the regime threshold, the setup is not actionable.

conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Trim zone: RSI above 70 / MFI above 80. Longer-timeframe readings carry more weight than short-term ones.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: VIX at 15.99, below its 50-day MA and out of the elevated regime, means moving-average support is once again reliable and risk appetite has normalized without stress.

conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A VIX spike into 25-30+ followed by a reversal lower is a high-quality re-entry signal; a correction without that spike should be treated as orderly rather than capitulative. Below 15 is a complacent regime.

primary_tension: A restored technical skeleton (50-day above a rising 200-day, +6.63% extension, full fib-cluster reclaim, VIX 15.99, Low exhaustion, credit neutral-tight) is colliding with the weakest confirmation set of the entire arc: McClellan breadth at its 856.63 cycle-low reference and net new highs at 1.18 while price rallies four straight days, ERP compressed to 0.32% in the valuation-ceiling band on a 4.745% 10-year, 5-day MFI already at ~83 in the trim zone, no capitulation VIX spike to validate the low, and Monte Carlo still 56.08% down-first — failing the 70% Late Bull threshold for a seventh consecutive session.
